South Korean Real Estate Industry Reels as Debt Crisis Escalates

South Korea’s real estate sector is facing mounting pressure as a deepening debt crisis disrupts property firms, ongoing projects, and employment across the industry. The crisis was triggered by a sudden tightening of credit markets last month, leaving real estate developers and agencies struggling to refinance maturing debts and secure new funding.

According to the Korea Real Estate Federation, more than 37% of mid-sized property firms have reported being unable to service upcoming loan repayments. “We’re seeing defaults rise at a pace not witnessed since the early 2000s,” said federation spokesperson Park Min-kyu. “The lack of liquidity is paralyzing operations industry-wide.”

Several large-scale residential and commercial projects in Seoul, Busan, and Incheon have been halted indefinitely due to cash flow shortages. “Our site has been idle for three weeks,” said Choi Eun-jung, a site manager in Gyeonggi Province. “Many of our workers have been furloughed, and we don’t know when construction can resume.”

The Korea Real Estate Workers Union estimates that over 9,000 industry jobs have been affected in the last month, with forced unpaid leave and layoffs becoming increasingly common. “Workers are anxious about their future, as companies cut costs to survive,” stated union president Kim Dong-hyun.

Industry analysts warn the crisis could persist if funding channels remain frozen. “Unless there is immediate intervention to restore credit flows, the situation will worsen for property firms and their employees,” said Lee Hae-jin of Seoul Market Analytics. The full impact on the industry remains uncertain as the crisis continues to unfold.
